text:
Maya: Quick sync — large customer just signed a PO asking for private deployment + audit logs + 99th pctl latency <= 120ms for api calls. They want launch in 7 weeks. Can we map dependencies and call out inevitable tradeoffs?

Sam: 7 weeks is tight. Need infra for VPC peering + Dedicated capacity, runtime changes for KV caching behavior at low latency, and a security review. Which of these are blockers vs. nice-to-have?

Priya: Runtime notes — to hit 120ms we need to: 1) pin an optimized kernel path (quantized) 2) disable some large prefix batching for this customer (will increase cost) 3) pre-warm KV cache and reserve warm slots. That’s ~2–3w dev+validation if we don’t already have the pinned kernel for their model.

Carlos: Infra timeline: VPC + firewall rules + peering request typically 5 business days once we have CIDR and infra account. Provisioning Dedicated fleet and GPUs depends on capacity availability — worst-case 3w lead time to get stable nodes in the pool. We can queue for burst capacity earlier.

Zoe: Security gets an initial review in 3 business days after we drop the control plane diagram and data flow. Full penetration / compliance artifacts (audit logs, KMS integration) are 2–3w depending on vendor KMS SLA. Also need to confirm whether keys live customer-side or we manage.

Maya: Customer requires customer-managed KMS and full request/response logging (audit logs stored 7 years). They’re regulated. So Zoe’s timeline applies.

Leo: From delivery POV: we should define clear launch gates — (A) infra + KMS + peering done, (B) runtime perf validated on canary traffic, (C) security sign-off with audit artifacts, (D) rollout plan + rollback hooks. Which of these can we parallelize?

Sam: (A) & (B) are coupled because runtime validation needs dedicated infra. But Carlos can start infra prep (CIDR, accounts, quota) in parallel with our kernel work. We should run a micro-canary on a small GPU instance early.

Priya: Agreed. My proposed split: Week 1–2: infra prep + kernel implementation + simple perf harness. Week 3: canary perf tests + KV pre-warm tuning. Week 4: security gating + long-tail logging verification. Week 5: final rollout + monitoring handover. That’s optimistic.

Carlos: We can front-load quota requests and reserve nodes in Week 1. If procurement approves burst nodes, we can get fleet by start of Week 3. I’ll raise the capacity ticket today.

Zoe: To avoid blocking, provide the control plane diagram and KMS flow by EOD. Also add a sample retention policy for logs and the S3 bucket ARNs. If customer manages keys, we need the KMS policy template filled.

Maya: I’ll get the diagram + KMS policy fields from the customer and share today. Also: CUSTOMER asked for an SLA addendum for latency — legal says we should avoid hard SLA until we validate performance. Can we propose a performance-based SLA with staged targets?

Sam: Yes — propose staged SLA: canary period (no SLA), Interim SLA (95th pctl guarantee), Post-validation SLA (99th pctl guarantee). That gives us runway to tune.

Leo: For rollout, recommend canary ratio start at 2% traffic with automatic rollback if errors > 0.5% or latency regression > 10% vs baseline. Monitoring: send traces and per-route latency into Console dashboards and alert on token-level cost spikes.

Priya: Adding the runtime config snippet for canary policy we discussed:
```yaml
canary:
  ratio: 0.02
  rollback_conditions:
    - error_rate: 0.005
    - latency_p99_delta: 0.10
metrics_export:
  - console_route: /customer/ACME
  - level: token_level
```
(we'll swap /customer/ACME for org id)

Carlos: Noted. Also need to confirm network egress paths for audit log delivery — will go direct S3 over VPC endpoint. Need customer to confirm bucket and IAM principal.

Zoe: Also note: long retention raises e-discovery considerations. Security will need an access matrix and approved people list for logs.

Maya: OK action items: 1) Maya — get CIDR, KMS choice, bucket ARNs, approved log access list (today) 2) Carlos — submit capacity + peering ticket (today) 3) Priya — start kernel optimization + perf harness (this week) 4) Sam — plan canary infra + rollback scripts + perf tests (this week) 5) Zoe — start security review once diagram + KMS flow exist (in 3 business days) 6) Leo — own rollout playbook + staged SLA language (this week).

Sam: One risk callout: if kernel pin requires upstream vendor patches, that could add 2–4w. We should define fallback: use a slightly larger instance class to meet latency but at higher cost. Need approval to spend on bigger nodes if we must.

Maya: Customer is price-conscious but values latency. I'll flag the fallback cost bucket in the PO negotiation — get their sign-off to allow temporary higher node-class during validation.

Leo: We should also scope what we cut if timeline slips: nonessential telemetry, non-mandatory RBAC features, and deferred model quantization work. Keep audit and KMS.

Priya: Agreed. And for test coverage, we'll include a prompt set that mimics their peak sequence lengths and a synthetic concurrency test.

deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline status: no active deployments. Queue created for dedicated-fleet request #DF-2241 by Carlos. Estimated provisioning ETA: 15 business days (subject to quota).

Carlos: I pushed DF-2241 and requested expedited procurement. Will update in thread when approved.

Maya: Thanks all. Let’s reconvene in 48h with updates. If anyone hits a blocker that affects the critical path, @here please escalate immediately. :thumbsup:

Sam: Acknowledged.

Priya: Acknowledged — will post perf baseline by EOD Friday.

Zoe: Acknowledged — will start checklist and share required artifact templates.
